reference_title: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures, 1993 Edition
chapter_title: Part II, Chapter 4 -- Low-Volume Road Design

sections.title: Design Chart Procedures and Design Catalog
sections.summary: A simplified special category for pavements subject to a relatively small number of heavy loads: flexible and rigid pavements use simplified chart procedures (Section 4.1.1), aggregate-surfaced roads use their own procedure incorporating aggregate loss and rutting criteria (Section 4.1.2); a design catalog (Section 4.2) of pre-solved typical designs is also provided for flexible, rigid, and aggregate-surfaced roads, streamlining low-volume-road design without requiring the full input-by-input Chapter 3 procedure.
sections.body: Chapter 4 (condensed here; printed guide pdf_page ~158-176, printed II-69 to II-87) provides a low-volume-road-specific alternative to the full Chapter 3 structural design procedure: simplified design charts for flexible and rigid pavements (Section 4.1.1) and for aggregate-surfaced roads (Section 4.1.2, incorporating the rutting and aggregate-loss performance criteria of Sections 2.2.2/2.2.3), plus a design catalog (Section 4.2, subsections 4.2.1 flexible, 4.2.2 rigid, 4.2.3 aggregate-surfaced) of representative pre-solved designs for typical low-volume-road conditions. This category applies to pavements subjected to a relatively small number of heavy load applications, where the full reliability/input-sensitivity of the Chapter 3 procedure is less critical.
key_points: Special design category for pavements with a relatively small number of heavy loads
Simplified design charts for flexible, rigid, and aggregate-surfaced roads (Section 4.1)
Design catalog of pre-solved typical designs (Section 4.2) for each pavement type
Aggregate-surfaced road design incorporates the rutting (Section 2.2.2) and aggregate-loss (Section 2.2.3) performance models
sections.applicability: Low-volume road design as a simplified alternative to the full Chapter 3 procedure; not individually digitized as callable functions in this module (the underlying Chapter 3 design equations and Section 2.2.2/2.2.3 aggregate-loss models ARE digitized and remain applicable).
